description:
LOCATION: crate-jmap-contacts-server/src/backend.rs:82-98

SIGNATURE:
    fn copy_contact_card(
        &self,
        caller: &Self::CallerCtx,
        from_account_id: &jmap_types::Id,
        to_account_id: &jmap_types::Id,
        card: jmap_contacts_types::ContactCard,
    ) -> impl Future<
        Output = Result<
            (jmap_types::Id, jmap_contacts_types::ContactCard),
            BackendSetError<Self::Error>,
        >,
    > + Send;

PROBLEM:
The `card: jmap_contacts_types::ContactCard` parameter (by value) ties
this trait method to the specific `ContactCard` type defined in the
sibling `jmap-contacts-types` crate. If a future workspace revision:

1. Splits ContactCard into a wire type (in jmap-contacts-types) and a
   domain type (e.g. ContactCardDomain in a new crate), or
2. Cuts a major version of jmap-contacts-types that changes
   ContactCard's public field set, or
3. Generalises copy across more types (e.g. for the metadata extension),

…this signature cannot move without breaking every ContactsBackend
implementor. Backend impls cannot use their own internal Card
representation through the trait either; they must accept the workspace
ContactCard shape.

Compared with the trait's other write methods (create_object,
update_object, destroy_object), which are generic over `O: SetObject +
Send + Sync`, this method is concrete. The shape inconsistency forces
callers into a mixed mode: use generic dispatch for /set,
concrete-typed dispatch for /copy. The workspace has chosen the
generic-over-O approach as canonical (matches RFC 8620 §6.3, where
/copy is a per-type method but the wire format is symmetric); copy is
the outlier.

WHAT CALLERS CANNOT DEPEND ON:
- That a future ContactCard schema change in jmap-contacts-types will
  not force a matching breaking change in this trait.
- That a backend can store cards in its own internal representation
  without first materializing them as `jmap_contacts_types::ContactCard`.

ASSESSMENT (P3, not higher):
The trait is workspace-internal and the types crate is a sibling that
will rev in lockstep with this crate. The version-skew failure mode
is hypothetical pre-1.0. The cookie-cutter inconsistency with the
generic-over-O write methods is the real engineering basis for the
flag.

RECOMMENDED:
Generalize the method:
    fn copy_object<O: SetObject + Send + Sync>(
        &self,
        caller: &Self::CallerCtx,
        from_account_id: &Id,
        to_account_id: &Id,
        obj: O,
    ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<(Id, O), BackendSetError<Self::Error>>> + Send;

The handler at card.rs:440-441 already deserializes to ContactCard,
applies the patch, then passes it through. The generic shape lets the
mail-server `/copy` (RFC 8621 §5.4 Email/copy) share the same trait
method via the canonical-template propagation rule.

PROPAGATION: jmap-mail-server has a concrete `copy_email` with the
same shape (`card: ContactCard` ↔ `email: Email`). The cookie-cutter
is internally consistent — both extensions have a concrete-typed
copy. Unifying both into a generic `copy_object` is a workspace-level
decision; file a workspace bead before sweeping if accepted.
title: ContactsBackend::copy_contact_card takes ContactCard by value, locking trait to the concrete jmap-contacts-types crate version
